clusters.mechanism: The tried-implementer exclusion is applied only on the escalation round, so later rounds pass only a preference for the current implementer and routing can return to an earlier exhausted implementer when the current one becomes unavailable.

Pinned verify chains clear every excludeModels constraint, which also removes the environment-blocked retry's exclusion of the first verifier, so the retry reruns the same verifier instead of the next chain entry.
The pinned-chain warning hardcodes the implementer's vendor/checkpoint as the reason, so it misattributes the cause when the avoided model or vendor is a previous verifier or a panel finder.

In panel review mode with a one-entry review chain, every finder routes to that model and the verifier's hard excludeModels removes it, leaving no eligible verifier and sending the run to needs_human.
The `!chain` condition disables the last-resort decline result for pinned chains, so a pinned decision model's usable last-resort answer is discarded and the run goes to needs_human.
Chain mode gives every candidate rank 0, so independence is not used to break ties between `|` alternatives.
